newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Frost-free outlook remains for Brazil coffee-Somar.
newsitem.headline: Frost-free outlook remains for Brazil coffee-Somar.

text.p: Brazil's coffee regions should see cooler weather over the weekend but there are no forecasts for damaging cold, local metereologists Somar said in an update Wednesday.

A polar air mass of 1,028 millibars will pass through the southern region of Brazil on the evening of July 4, leading to a fall in temperatures in north Parana state to around four degrees Celsius, said Somar forecaster Marcos Massari.

The colder weather will spread to more northern coffee areas from the evening of July 5 but as the center of the air mass will already be heading out to the ocean, the periphery which will reach the coffee areas will be humid, Somar said.
Minimum temperatures in southern Minas Gerais and north Sao Paulo states should be no less than five degrees Celsius and no frosts are forecast.
Temperatures will start to pick up again from the early morning of July 9, Massari said.
U.S weather services also see no damaging cold in sight for Brazilian coffee areas over the next seven days.
